questions.question:

questions.solution:
The correct answer is “**To be extremely happy”.**

• The idiom "on cloud nine" is a common phrase used to express a state of extreme happiness or euphoria. 
 
• The phrase does not relate to being cautious, shaky, or sad in any way, ruling out the other options as they do not align with the sentiment of elation.
 
• The imagery of being on "cloud nine" suggests a blissful, worry-free state that is visually represented by being elevated above the ordinary, every day concerns.

Hence, the correct answer is ‘**Option 2’.**

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The rebels __laid up__ their arms.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **“laid down”.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• "Laid down their arms" is a common phrase indicating to surrender or cease fighting, by literally putting down weapons. 
 
• "Laid up" suggests being confined or put away for storage or repair, which does not fit the context of stopping conflict or hostilities.
 
• "Laid out", "laid on", and "laid by" have different meanings: planning or arranging, applying, and saving, respectively, none of which properly express the intended notion of cessation of conflict.
 
• "Laid down" is a widely recognized and historically utilized expression that clearly communicates the idea of surrender or truce.

Hence, the correct answer is ‘**Option 1**’.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

______ UK government continually reiterates its commitment to halting the brain drain.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is “**The**”.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• "**The**" is used before singular or plural nouns and noun phrases that denote particular, specified persons or things.
 
• In this context, "The UK government" specifies a particular government of a country, making "The" the only suitable option.
 
• "A", "An", and "Any" are articles used in more general contexts or where the noun is not specifically defined, which does not apply to the unique entity of the UK government.
 
• Using "The" also emphasizes the unique status of the UK government in this context, highlighting its specific actions or policies.

Hence, the correct answer is ‘**Option 1’**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 2: "**A**" - This would imply that there are multiple UK governments, which is not the intended meaning of the sentence. It doesn't convey the specificity needed in this context.
 
• Option 3: "**An**" - "An" is used before words that begin with a vowel sound. Since "UK" begins with a consonant sound ("yoo-kay"), "an" is not appropriate here.
 
• Option 4: "**Any**" - This doesn't convey the specific identity of the UK government. It implies a more general statement, which is not the intended meaning.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

The teacher said, “She had started the fight”.

options.text: The teacher complained that she has started the fight.
The teacher said that she had started the fight.
The teacher ordered that she had started the fight,
The teacher said that she has started the fight.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is “**The teacher said that she had started the fight.”**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• This option accurately converts the direct speech into reported speech without changing the tense of the original action verb "had started," which is already in past perfect and should remain unchanged in reported speech.
 
• It maintains the original statement's integrity by correctly attributing the action (starting the fight) to the same subject without misinterpreting or adding unintended connotations like "complained" or “ordered”.
 
• The sentence structure is a direct application of the rules of changing direct speech into indirect (reported) speech, showing that when the reporting verb is in the past tense, the tense of the direct statement usually does not change if it is already in a past form.
 
• By choosing "said" as the reporting verb, the sentence preserves the neutrality of the original statement without implying any additional attitude or emotion.

Hence, the correct answer is ‘**Option 2’.**

“He was holding the earrings up to his ears now, turning them this way and that, pursing his lips, playing at girlishness.”

What do you infer as the most probable reason for Achilles’ behaviour?

options.text: Achilles was selecting an ideal gift for Lycomedes.
Achilles was in charge of selecting the best accessories for war.
Achilles was in a woman’s disguise and was playing his part.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is “**Achilles was in a woman’s disguise and was playing his part”.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Achilles examining earrings and experimenting with perfume suggests an engagement with items not traditionally associated with his warrior persona, indicating he’s embodying a different role. 
 
• The act of holding earrings up to his ears and "playing at girlishness" directly points towards Achilles adopting feminine attire or behavior, rather than selecting gifts for someone else or focusing on war preparation.
 
• The historical context of Achilles being hidden in a woman’s disguise to avoid going to the Trojan War, as told in various myths, supports the inference that he is in disguise here, playing his part convincingly.
 
• This behavior does not align with the responsibilities of selecting war accessories (Option 2) or acting as an ideal host (Option 4), but directly indicates his disguise and the act of blending into his assumed role.

Hence, the correct answer is **‘Option 3’**.
